Sam — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from today’s discovery so we keep momentum toward the POC (target start: Oct 5).

Call recap (30m):
- Use case: real-time chat summarization + search re-ranking for clinical notes ingestion. Expected peak spikes during end-of-day processing windows.
- Primary success metrics you mentioned: 95th pct latency < 300ms for short-chat flows, < 600ms for long summaries; inference cost per 1k tokens target <$0.12; throughput to support 120 RPS sustained with bursts to 600 RPS for 30–90s.
- Data sensitivity: PHI present — you want Private deployment in AWS GovCloud or VPC with customer KMS; we flagged our Private onboarding checklist.

Proposed immediate actions (owner in parens):
1) Traffic intake: Veridian to send a sample of request traces + token-length distribution and 48-hour RPS CSV (Sam/Priya) — due Sep 13.
2) Redwood to validate fit & propose model/quantization and a brief mutual action plan (Jordan/Karthik) — draft by Sep 15.
3) Security intake: Veridian to complete the initial security questionnaire stub (Priya) — Sep 17.
4) POC success criteria & owners: Redwood to propose measurable acceptance tests (latency, error rate, quality regression on provided eval set) and pair with Veridian owners for sign-off (Monica/Ben).

Attachments: I attached a small traffic_characteristics.csv template and an action-plan workbook (mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx). Please confirm who will own the traffic export and whether the 600 RPS burst estimate is peak concurrent or aggregated across pods.

Next meeting: propose Sep 16, 10:00am PT to review traffic and the draft M A P. Let me know if that works.

— Jordan

Subject: Re: Next steps: Veridian POC traffic & acceptance criteria

Sam — thanks for the samples. I pulled some quick stats and a few follow-ups we’ll need to firm up the POC plan: 

Immediate intake items we need by EOD Sep 15 (to lock the POC window Oct 5–Nov 5):
1) 48hr RPS CSV format: please include timestamp, endpoint, response_token_count, request_token_count, response_status. The CSV you sent is mostly good — missing response_token_count for a small portion. If you can patch that, we’ll run a synthetic replay locally. (owner: Veridian)
2) Token-length buckets: confirm percentiles for request and response tokens (P10, P50, P90, P95, P99) — sample from the attached payloads or provide a small histogram file. (owner: Veridian)

POC acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Latency: 95th pct end-to-end inference < 300ms for short flows (<= 256 tokens request + <= 128 tokens response).
- Latency: 95th pct < 600ms for long summaries (<= 1,800 tokens combined).
- Throughput: sustain 120 RPS with <1% error, tolerate bursts to 600 RPS for 60s with graceful degradation (queued or fallback to cheaper model).
- Cost: inference unit economics below $0.14 per 1k output tokens on average (we’ll report measured cost during POC).
- Quality: no regression > 5% on your 250-example eval set (we’ll run both our eval harness and your labels).

Run plan:
- Phase 0 (prep): replay of 48hr trace on small cluster to validate profile — week Sep 21–24.
- Phase 1 (baseline): run unoptimized hosted model to get baseline latency/cost — week Sep 27–Oct 1.
- Phase 2 (opt & iterate): test batching/quantization and routing policies — Oct 5–Oct 22.
- Phase 3 (acceptance): joint validation against acceptance tests — Oct 23–Oct 30.

Owners on Redwood side: Jordan (customer coordination & MAP), Karthik (runtime & benchmarks), Ben (deployment & infra tuning), Monica (quality evals). Please confirm Veridian owners for each of the acceptance test lines so we can put them in the MAP.

One operational Q: are we okay to use a staging bucket in your AWS account for the 48hr replay logs (we will request temporary access) or should Redwood host the replay artifacts? Either is fine — we prefer your bucket for fidelity.

— Karthik
Director, Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
